title: Getting in there for my dream card game. Now working on a dynamic arena.
author: xcantene
selftext:
I've been working on my game Hunt Protocol for almost a year now!

It's a fast-paced card hunting game where you fight monsters and can even compete against other players at the same time. The game itself is now working, so I've been spending more time improving effects, animations, and creating new 3D models.

One thing I really wanted was to make an arena that actually reacts to what happens during the fight and the cards you play.

So far, I've managed to create dynamic grass that reacts to monster roars and stomps, terrain that gets cracks and marks from attacks, and even grass that can catch on fire or freeze!

The video shows some examples of what I've been working on. I'm still trying to improve everything and give the arena more personality.

At the end, you can also see a full 3D world I've been building for Legendary cards. When you play one of these cards, it triggers a cinematic in that world. It's definitely not perfect yet, but I'm pretty happy with how it's starting to look!

For those curious about my AI workflow:

I mostly work with Codex and Opus 5.5. I use Codex to help generate reference images for my models, research how different creatures move and behave, and work through multiple screenshots to figure things out.

Codex then helps me build a basic version and creates documentation that I pass to Opus 5.5 to rework and improve.

I've also built my own little 3D modeling studio where I can edit positions, spines, and animations without needing to constantly use Blender. I can go in and make changes myself, while Codex also helps me create vector art that Opus can animate directly on the terrain.

So far, pretty much every animation has taken me around a day because I keep going back and polishing things until I'm happy with them. 😅

There's still a lot I want to improve, but I thought I'd share what I've managed to build so far! What do you think still could use even more work in your opinion?
